note: The release plan for the Product & Program page. Milestones hold stories, stories hold an estimate in days of work, and every date on the page is computed from what is still outstanding — nothing here is a hand-typed date (the CEO's ruling, 2026-09-04). Releases run in the order listed; each one's estimated date is the previous one's plus its own remaining work. A release with unestimated stories has no date, and neither does anything after it, because a chain built on a guess is worse than an honest blank. Seeded 2026-09-05: v0.2.0's stories are the real remaining requirements of its two critical projects; everything after it is a placeholder waiting to be sketched with the CEO. Re-scoped 2026-09-09: v0.2.1 is the Mark III, the robot that learns; the entry named 'Machines that pay for themselves' is parked off the plan by the CEO (the name was cryptic and unhelpful) and M3's content waits to be re-sketched with him.

releases.name: Player Update 1.1
releases.contains: The Mark III, the first robot that learns. You buy it, put it down, and it works out how to water your field by trying: clumsy for a few days, better every morning. Plus the fresh-player evidence v0.2.0 shipped without (one unprompted adult session on the tablet, the sleeping-cot and standing bars scored from its trace). The ripe-crop glance and the bed outline made the v0.2.0 tag after all and are listed here as done.

stories.title: Build what the robot is told before each decision — its tile, its energy, a 5×5 view — as an adjustable spec
Write the reward table and the policy: a linear softmax with a REINFORCE trace, deterministic under the sim's seed
Give the Mark III its day: the learn setting in the bot brain, one decision a second, parks on an empty meter
Update its weights at the day turn, keep them in the save, and prove a day replays to its autosave with the weights intact
Put Robot Mk III in the shop with its own sprite, and let its panel say days practised and yesterday's score
The learning-curve demo and its test: the same seed for seven days, the score rises, two runs are identical
Watch it on the tablet: it learns within a week of in-game days, and what it is doing can be said out loud
Give it the hoe: a till action, a bare-soil channel and a 0.1 reward, so a fresh robot can earn by accident on open ground
stories.why: Ruled 2026-09-09 (Q-99) after the demo showed a fresh robot walking off the field before it earned anything.

stories.title: One unprompted first session by an adult who has never played, on the tablet
Score the sleeping-cot bar from that session's trace: at least one sleep, unprompted
Confirm no regression on the standing bars — dead taps at or under 12%, longest stall at or under 16.3 seconds
A ripe crop is obvious at a glance
stories.why: From play, 2026-09-07: nothing on the farm said loudly enough that a plant was ready to pick — she had to go looking. Measured, the ripe cell repaints most of the plant (38 of 56 pixels) and still cannot be seen, because it changes brightness by 0.3 of 255 and barely moves the outline — a hue shift inside one family, and hue is the first thing distance throws away. Five candidates were built and judged on the tablet from two staged sheets, one at ground level and one from the height the camera rises to when she is directing a robot. Ruled 2026-09-08 (Q-94): a ready plant sways gently and gives off its own ripe colour — gold under wheat, red under tomato. Shipped as the only behaviour, wordless (S-7), and it cannot touch the sim (D-8).

stories.title: Fix the bed outline left over from the cot moving indoors
stories.why: Reported from play 2026-09-07 — "at nighttime, when all of your energy is spent, look at the house from the outside". The dusk cue lights the tile the next tap should land on, and it always drew the bed's own 16x32 footprint: on the 16x16 front door that spilled onto the wall above, so the house wore a bed outline every evening. Fixed the same day — the shape is now a pure function in `CotPresentation` and asserted, rather than inline geometry nobody could test.

releases.name: Towers and waves
releases.contains: The tower-defense slice. Towers that start out taking orders and end up running themselves, and waves designed against the simulation rather than by hand.

releases.name: A bot that learns from you
releases.contains: The fuller learning slice: a bot you can show, trained on your own recorded sessions, with the overnight training loop running on the tablet itself at fleet scale. The first learned bot arrives earlier, as v0.2.1's Mark III.
